3. That on 12.03.2008 the present Respondent No.1, as plaintiff, instituted other Suit No.39 of 2008 in the Court of Joint District Judge, Patiya, Chittagong, impleading defendant-appellant and others, for declaration that the "will" in dispute and "probate" thereof granted under order No.87 dated 19.07.2007 passed in Miscellaneous case No.27 of 1998 and probate Certificate issued on 16.09.2007 in respect of "Kha" schedule land are forged, collusive and void with further declaration that his (Plaintiffs) purchase Deeds No.3811, 3812 and 3813 all dated 02.08.2007 executed by defendant No.9 and registered on 02.08.2007 are genuine and valid. It is stated that the land described in schedule "Ka" to the plaint was owned by Sudhindra Nath Chowdhury alias Sudhir Nath Chowdhury who died leaving behind three sons namely Ashutosh Chowhury, Sontosh Chowdhury and Babul Chowdhury (defendant-respondent, No.7 to 9) and three daughter and as such each son became the Owner and possessor of 1/3rd share of the 'Ka' schedule land as he daughters did not inherit any property as per Hindu law of inheritance that while in possession and enjoyment of the same in the above manner Babul Chandra Chowdhury (Defendant-respondent No.9) sold 06.00 acre of land to the plaintiff by three registered deeds of sale being Nos.3811, 3812, and 3813 all dated 02.08.2007 and handed over possession of the same as described in schedule 'Kha' to the plaint: that it is alleged while the plaintiff was possessing his purchased land, defendant No.1, (appellant herein) on 18.11.2007 at 9.30 a.m. hired some miscreants and forcibly tried to encroach upon the 'Kha' scheduled land but failed that at one stage when the said defendant was returning back from the suit land, she disclosed that she got the said land through a will, executed by her father on 12.03.1993 pursuant to which probate was granted in Miscellaneous Case No.27 of 1998 (Probate) that after having come to know about the same from Nurul Islam, his caretaker, the plaintiff went to the Court and upon enquiry came to know about the probate case ; that thereafter upon obtaining the certified copy of the same the plaintiff Became sure about the order passed in the said probate case and issuance of probate certificate; that the plaintiff also came to know from the local people that defendant No.1, never resided in the locality where the suit land is situated and rather she used to reside in the town that he also came to know that amongst the three sons of deceased Sudhindra Nath Chowdhury two sons, Ashutosh Chowdhury and Shontosh Chowdhury (defendant Nos.7 and 8) left Bangladesh after the liberation war and Sudhindra Nath chowhdury used to reside with his youngest son Babul Chowdhury (defendant No.9), that while Sudhindra became very sick he was shifted to India for better treatment in the month of March, 1997 and he stayed there with his two other sons (defendant No.7 and 8) and ultimately he died there on 13.04.1997 due to ailment and all his funeral ceremonies were performed in India, that seine Sudhindra at the fag end of his life and before going to India stayed with defendant No.9 in Bangladesh, it was unusual to execute a will in favour of the defendant No.1, when he was living with Babul his son that thus the story of executed by will is nothing but a bundle of leas which was created by forging he signature of Sudhindra Nath Chowdhury @ Sudhir in Collusion with defendant Nos.2-6, who by practicing fraud upon the Court obtained the Probate Certificate beyond the Knowledge of the legal heirs of the testator. In that view of the matter those documents are null and void. Hence the suit has been filed by the plaintiff. 

 8. Mr. Rokanuddin Mahmud the learned Senior Advocate appearing on behalf of the defendant-appellant submits that the procedure and power of granting or revoking probate of a will is specially delegated power given to particular Court by the statute and since in the present case after observing due process of law the probate of the will has been granted the same or the will cannot be declared null and void by a ordinary civil court nor a person not interested in the estate of the testator an a such filing a declaratory suit invoking jurisdiction under section 42 of the specific Relief Act is barred by law. He next submits that both the courts below failed to appreciate that the plaintiff being not an interested person through the testator in the estate of the deceased testator can another challenge the will nor the probate in any court as the same is expressly barred by law specially section 263 of the succession Act. Thus the trial Court as well as the High Court Division erred in not rejecting the plaint as barred by law. He then submits that the High Court Division in deciding the revision failed to comprehend that the plaint itself disclose non maintainability of the suit and that the probate of will was granted under a special law and the suit filed to declare the will and the probate to be null and void under specific Relief Act is of Completely civil nature and that the special law overrides the general jurisdiction conferred on civil Courts to entertain the suit of civil nature and as such the suit is impliedly barred and a suit which is barred by law should not be decided on taking evidence as the settled principle of law is that no fruitless litigation should be allowed to continue which prima facie appears to be barred by law or in any manner deemed to be ended without any result and hence by refusing to reject the plaint both courts committed error in the decision resulting in failure of justice. 

 10. From the materials on record and the submission of the learned advocate for both the parties it appears that the moor question is whether the suit instituted in the Court of learned Joint District Judge praying for declaration that the will in question dated 12.03.1993 is forged concocted inactive and null and void and accordingly pro-bate granted on the basis of the said will by order No.84 dated 19.07.2007 in Miscellaneous Case No.27 of 1998 (Probate) is baseless inactive, invalid and null and Void is maintainable on the face of section 263 of the succession Act. 

 11. From the submissions of the learned advocate for the appellant it appears that on the basis of the will dated 12.03.1993 probate case was filed and the same was disposed of granting probate in Miscellaneous Case No. 27 of 1998 (Probate). The law provides that once probate is granted in respect of a will by a competent Court the will becomes acted upon and challenging of the same after probate is granted also hits the validity of the probate which under all circumstance if allowed ultimately the probate granted by inappropriate court having jurisdiction to deal with the same will stand revoked. 

 b) the grant was obtained fraudulently by making a false suggestion or by cancelling from the court something material to the case ; or 

 13. From the above it is clear that when the probate is granted it become an order of the Court Revocation of the same can only done on the basis of just cause as defined in the said section. From the facts and circumstance of the case. It appears that the plaintiff claims that the will in question is product of forgery and fraud and as such the same is illegal and void. The allegation thus attracts illustration No.3 of the section as mentioned above which, if proved, would be a " just cause" under Explanation (b) of section 263 of the Succession Act and as such the probate may be revoked. Thus section 263 attracts the present case. Side by side on perusal of section 264 of he said Act it appears that the same empowers the learned District Judge to have jurisdiction in granting's the revoking probate in all cases within his district which clearly oust the jurisdiction of all other Court's. Section 265 of the said Act empowers the Supreme Court to appoint such judicial officers within any Supreme Court to appoint such judicial officers within any district to act for the District Judge as Delegates probate and letters of administration within such local limits as may be prescribed and per-sons so appointed Shall be called "District Delegates" Section 266 of the said Act also provides that such District Delegates shall have the like powers and authority in relation to granting probate and letters of administration, and all matters connected therewith as are by law vested upon him in relation to any civil suit or proceeding pending in his Court. 

 14. Reading all the aforesaid provisions of law it is clear that after granting probate by the competent Court if any question is raised in respect of an will on the basis of which probate was granted and if in such case the will is disturbed it shall make the probate revoked which is within the domain of the specially empowered Court and thereby a Civil Court under the Civil Courts Act shall have no jurisdiction to adjudicative/determine the same. The learned District Judge or the District Delegate being empowered to deal with such matters is the only authority who can either grant or revoke the same. Moreover, when the District Judge or District Delegates being specially empowered by law granted probate of a will after observing due process of law the same cannot be interfered with or declared null and void on the prayer of a person, not interested through the testator in the estate of the deceased testator, by filing a simple declaratory suit invoking jurisdiction under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. So far the plaintiffs claim is concerned he is to prove that he is interested in the estate of the deceased testator through the testator and that also is to be proved before the appropriate Court having competent jurisdiction. 

 16. When relief has been provided for is particular statute in the present case under succession Act discretionary power granted under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act cannot be invoked. 

 17. Thus under such circumstances the statute debars the ordinary civil Court to make such declaration. In the instant case when the plaintiff sought for declaration that the will other basis of which the probate has been granted is null and void being forged and concocted the result of such declaration if allowed will affect the certificate of probate and seeking of further relief then a more declaration of title cannot make further relief in that suit inasmuch as declaring the will void shall automatically revoke the probate granted by the competent Court whenever the probate granted by a competent Court is affected or someone disputes the basis of granting such probate which will make the probate revoked the cannot institute any suit under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act but to invoke relief as provided for under section 263 and 264 of the Succession Act 1925 because by granting probate all the movable and immovable properties of the deceased has become conclusive. 

 18. In the case of Chiranjilal Shrilal Goenka Vs. Jasjit singh and others repotted in (1993) 2 Supreme Court Case 503 the Indian Supreme Court, relying on he case of Ishwardeo Narain Singh Vs. Smt Kamta Devi reported in AIR 1954 SC 280 held " the Court of probate is only concerned with the question as to whether the document put forward as the last will and testament of a deceased person was duly executed and attested in accordance with law and whether at the time of such exaction the testator had sound dispersing mind Therefore the only issue in probate proceedings relates to the genuineness and due execution of will and the court itself is under duty to determine it and preserve the original will in its custody. The succession Act is self contained code insofar as the question of making an application for probate grant or refusal of probate or an appeal carried against the decision of the probate court. This is clearly manifest in the fascicule of the provision of the Act" Thus the probate Court has been concerned with exclusive jurisdiction to grant probate of the will of the deceased annexed to the petition on the granting or refusal thereof it has to preserve the original will produced before it. The grant of probate is final subject to appeal if any or revocation if made in terms of the provisions of the succession Act. In the said judgment it has further been held granting of probate "is a judgment in rem and conclusive and binds not only the parties but also the entire world. The award depraves the parties of statutory right of appeal provided under the provision of succession act" 

 19. From the above since granting of probate is a judgment in rem and binds not only he parties but also to the entire world any question relating to the will after granting of "probate" cannot be looked into by any other civil court other than the court having competent jurisdiction ensured by the statue. In the other words the probate court alone has exclusive jurisdiction and the civil Court on original side does not have jurisdiction even if consented to by the parties, to adjudicate upon the proof or validity of he will propounded by the executrix once the probate is granted. In the instant case the suit instituted by the plaintiff was for declaration under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act for declaring the will forged, fraudulent invalid etc, such step of the plaintiff is misconceived because so long the probate stands, the plaintiff is not entitled to any legal character or any right to property as required by section 42 of he Specific Relief Act. The Court of Joint District Judge, was to therefore incompetent to proceed with the hearing and determining the present suit. A suit filed in a Court incompetent under the provision of an Act is not maintainable .When the suit is not maintainable it is nothing but a futile exercise which should not be a allowed to proceed with. As such the trial Court as well as the High Court Division committed serious error of law in rejecting the application under order VII Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Thus we are of the view that the application under order VII Rule 11 of the Coder was rightly filed by the defendant No.1, (appellant herein) and as such, the trial Court as well as the High Court Division committed serious illegality in rejecting such application of the defendant appellant.
